content:
Jamie Lee Curtis has rebuked social media users who took issue with her recent birthday post.

On her 68th birthday on Sunday, the “Halloween” star mourned that she was “the only surviving family member of my immediate family and my immediate second family” and therefore, “the last in the line.”

Her post featured photos of her parents, actors Tony Curtis and Janet Leigh, as well as her stepfather, Robert Brandt, and sister, Kelly, who died this year.

But some commenters criticized Curtis for excluding her living half-siblings from her dad’s later marriages — sisters Alexandra and Allegra and brother Ben.

“Oh my goodness, Internet,” she wrote. “Really? Is it such a slow news cycle that you have to turn this into a beef or me throwing shade? Come on. You know better than that. Or do you?”

The Oscar winner clarified that “immediate family means my immediate family,” meaning “my mother and my father and my sister Kelly and my stepfather who raised me.”

She also reassured everyone that her extended family is still very much a part of her life.

“My extended family, all of my father’s children from other marriages and all of their children and now their children’s children are fully intact and we all are in direct communication and we just celebrated a bar mitzvah and we all mourned together the loss of our Kelly, as we did our brother, Nicholas, but any attempt to try to make this into something it isn’t is just a silly waste of clickbait,” she said.

Curtis’ fans defended her in the comments section.

“Imagine having to explain to people what immediate family means,” one person wrote. “Also I find it insane that instead of focusing on sending love and well wishes when she has basically spelled out that she has had to live through a lot of grief just sums up how messed up this world has become.”

Another person commented, “It’s sad that you had to explain this.”

“The internet is always bored and looking for BS to blow out of proportion,’ someone else added.

In Curtis’ initial birthday post, she called her sibling’s death a “real blow.”

“I look back at photographs of me as a child, and I look so stunned to be here at birth, and it carried on through much of my young life, always seemingly startled and slightly concerned,” she added. “I’ve worked through a lot of that discomfort, and I’m so happy to be here and have the life I have. Both personal and creative.”
